title: AstronautBench: Measuring Agent Self-Improvement Across Episodes Through Knowledge, Evidence, and Progress
abstract: arXiv:2611.26910v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: LLM agents are expected to improve themselves from their own experience across episodes, with fixed weights. Self-improvement in an embodied world cannot be read from one measure. Existing benchmarks measure task progress, world-knowledge question answering (QA), and episodic memory, but a correct answer does not show that the agent ever observed the evidence for it, and progress does not show what the agent learned. We introduce AstronautBench, which measures one agent's self-improvement through three views on the same run: what it knows, whether its own evidence supports that knowledge, and how far it gets in the world. It is built on the game Outer Wilds, where each episode is a 22-minute loop after which the world resets, only the agent's knowledge carries over, and progress is gated by knowledge. translated_title: AstronautBench：通过知识、证据与进展衡量智能体跨回合的自我改进
translated_abstract: LLM智能体被期望在权重固定不变的情况下，从跨回合的自身经验中实现自我改进。具身世界中的自我改进无法通过单一指标来衡量。现有基准测试分别衡量任务进展、世界知识问答（QA）和情景记忆，但一个正确答案并不能表明智能体曾经观察到支持该答案的证据，而任务进展也无法表明智能体究竟学到了什么。我们提出了AstronautBench，它通过三个视角来衡量同一个智能体运行过程中的自我改进：它知道什么、它自身获得的证据是否支持这些知识、以及它在世界中取得了多大的进展。该基准建立在游戏《星际拓荒》之上，其中每个回合是一个22分钟的循环，循环结束后世界重置，只有智能体的知识得以保留，且世界中的进展由知识所限制。在每个回合结束后，我们测量到达的地点数量和飞船日志中揭示的传闻事实数量，以及关于164个问题的回答正确性……
tldr: AstronautBench基于游戏《星际拓荒》构建了一个新基准，通过知识、证据支持与任务进展三个互补视角，衡量权重固定的LLM智能体在世界不断重置的循环中凭借自身经验实现跨回合自我改进的能力。
en_tdlr: AstronautBench is a benchmark built on the game Outer Wilds that measures LLM agent self-improvement across episodes through three complementary views—knowledge, evidence support, and world progress—where only knowledge persists as the world resets every 22-minute loop.
